statements.body: The project owner is a freelance illustrator who personally experiences the problem.
Preparing invoices currently consumes the owner's evenings, representing meaningful lost personal time.
The owner already logs hours and expects that log to be the input for invoice generation.
The system must track payment status per invoice, distinguishing at minimum paid from unpaid.
The solution must run on shared hosting the owner already pays for.
The owner will not pay a recurring monthly fee for any SaaS tool to solve this problem.
What format or tool does the owner currently use to log hours, and what shape is that data in?
What does a completed invoice need to contain — line items, hourly rate, client details, tax, terms?
How many active clients and invoices per month does the owner typically manage?
What shared hosting environment is available — PHP version, database access, shell access, supported runtimes?
Whether the system needs to send invoices by email directly or only generate a downloadable file is not yet decided.

concerns.coverage: The owner spends evenings manually producing invoices from logged hours; without this project that time cost continues and payment tracking remains ad hoc.
A single freelance illustrator is the sole operator and beneficiary; there is no named secondary user or client-facing role yet.
Work enters as logged hours and exits as an invoice; payment tracking is a subsequent step, but intermediate handoffs and client communication steps are not yet described.
Hour logs and invoice records are the core data; client details and payment status must be stored, but schema, volume, and retention requirements are not yet specified.
Must run on existing shared hosting at no additional recurring cost; no SaaS subscriptions are acceptable.
Paying for external SaaS tooling is explicitly excluded; no other explicit non-goals have been stated yet.

candidates.body: What observable outcome would tell you this project worked — for example, invoicing an evening's work in under ten minutes, or zero invoices forgotten in a quarter?
candidates.whySelected: Success is the only uncovered core concern in the ledger; every other core area has at least partial coverage. Naming the observable evidence of success bounds how polished the first slice must be and prevents building past the point of usefulness.

candidates.body: In what format and tool do you currently log your hours, and can you share an example of what one logged entry looks like?
candidates.whySelected: The hour log is the declared input to the whole pipeline, and its shape is an approved unknown. Knowing whether it is a spreadsheet, paper, or an app determines the import mechanism for the first slice, but it fills no uncovered core concern.

candidates.body: What can your shared hosting actually run — which PHP version, database, and whether you have shell or cron access?
candidates.whySelected: The hosting constraint is hard and already approved, but its concrete capabilities are an open unknown; a wrong assumption here invalidates the entire technical approach. It bounds the slice's stack choices but does not fill the uncovered success concern.

readyAdvice.why: Success remains an uncovered core concern, and the two unknowns most likely to shape the first slice — the hour-log format and the hosting environment's capabilities — are still unanswered. Once success is defined and the input data shape is known, a first vertical slice could reasonably be scoped.

statements.body: Success requires that every hour logged in a given month is converted to a billed invoice within three days of month close.
Success requires a dashboard or summary view that shows outstanding client balances at a glance without manual calculation.

concerns.coverage: The project has worked when every month closes with all hours billed within three days and outstanding balances are visible at a glance — both are observable without ambiguity.

candidates.body: What format or tool do you currently use to log hours, and what does one entry look like (fields, granularity, per-client tagging)?
candidates.whySelected: The hour log is the sole input to invoice generation, and its shape is still an approved unknown (5507d80f). Nothing about the first vertical slice — parsing, invoicing, or the three-day month-close success metric — can be designed until the input's format and fields are known. This question bounds the import step, the data schema, and how much cleanup work the slice must absorb.

candidates.body: What does your shared hosting actually provide — PHP or other runtimes, database access, cron jobs, outbound email, and shell access?
candidates.whySelected: The hosting constraint (c6897472) is hard, but its concrete capabilities are an approved unknown (0fe129e3). The answer decides the entire technology envelope for the slice and also determines whether the still-undecided email-sending option (6fe43178) is even feasible, so it removes a large amount of design uncertainty at once.

candidates.body: What must a finished invoice contain — line items, hourly rate per client, your business and client details, tax handling, and payment terms?
candidates.whySelected: Invoice contents are an approved unknown (10589040) and define the output half of the first slice. However, the input format question bounds more of the pipeline, so this ranks below it: you can sketch an invoice template from examples, but you cannot parse a log you have never seen.

readyAdvice.why: All ten core concerns have some coverage and success is observable, but three approved unknowns sit directly on the first slice's critical path: the hour-log input format, the hosting environment's capabilities, and the invoice's required contents. Until at least the input format and hosting capabilities are answered, any build would rest on guesses about both ends of the pipeline.
